#143845. Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1520 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games.
  • It has been revealed that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95.
  • It has been revealed that microsoft, all the while, were taking notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.

It has been revealed that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95. At E3 later that May, Microsoft demonstrated the Strategic Commander for the first time with SimCity 3000, while promoting its potential for other such games as Diablo II, Warcraft III, and Baldur's Gate II. This was all taking place during the so-called 'Golden Age of Real-Time Strategy Games,' which spanned roughly from the mid-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was when the RTS genre was at the peak of its mainstream popularity, and we fans were devoted to mastering its intricacies in any way we could to have a competitive edge.

It has been revealed that microsoft, all the while, were taking notes. "The team conceived the Strategic Commander in the late 1990s," Carl Ledbetter - then Industrial Design Manager for Microsoft's PC Hardware Group, now Head of Design for Xbox Devices - recalls to me. "As RTS games grew in popularity, we saw an interesting opportunity to design a newly introduced physical interface around a new interaction model. The idea was for it to be used left-handed in concert with right-hand PC desktop mouse control. We wanted to enable players to perform faster with more fluidity, comfort, optimised control placement for multiple hand sizes, simplicity of set-up, and ease of programming.".

For Ledbetter and co. to realise this ambition, the Strategic Commander was designed as a unique combination of mouse, joystick, and gamepad. To manage the increasing complexities of the RTS games of the day, it came equipped with six programmable buttons, three shift buttons, and a three-position profile switch. Back then, these atypical features provided an unprecedented 72 possible key combinations across various configurations, all at the tip of our stubby little fingers. Better yet, it allowed us to toggle between three pre-configured profiles at a time, so that we could switch up our configurations on the fly depending on which stage of an RTS match we were in.

On release, contemporary reviewers acknowledged its originality, with critics like ActiveWin's Julien Jay describing it as "probably the most innovative (with the GameVoice) and revolutionary" peripheral designed specifically for strategy players. Others, like Neoseeker's Arnel Lim, suggested that it might’ve gone overboard with its customisation options, saying "you won't use anywhere close to all of them," in reference to the controller's programmable key combinations. Either way, the Strategic Commander failed to supplant conventional peripherals in the hands of most RTS players, and it was discontinued in 2003. As was the rest of the original SideWinder line, owing to declining sales and the industry-wide shift toward standard M+K setups for all PC games and genres.

However, unlike so many of its Microsoft-made siblings, this was not the end for the Strategic Commander. Niche as it was, it went on to enjoy a surprisingly long post-shelf life, one that was stretched out by a dedicated cult following - and that continues to this day. But why? Why, after all these years, is this forgotten peripheral from a discontinued line maintaining such a enthusiastic fanbase, years after the industry around it had written it off as a failure?

The answer lies in software and OS compatibility, as much as the hardware's own appeal. Andreas Weis was the developer of one of the first unofficial patches for the Strategic Commander, allowing players to keep on using it even after the original software stopped being compatible with newer versions the Windows. By that point, the device was a decade old, and well into 'official' obsolescence, yet Weis still answered the call of the Strategic Commander's righteously frustrated - if numerically few - fans. "There was a lot of interest back in the early 2010s in software patches to keep the Strategic Commander functional when the original software for the Strategic Commander stopped working," he explains. "Consumers were asking around on internet forums about how to get it to work on Windows 7 and Vista machines. Since I was studying computer science at the time, I was quite interested in reverse-engineering, and I hacked together a simple tool that would cover my use cases for the device.".

According to recent reports, in the years that followed, other patches were released to keep the Strategic Commander operational, the most notable of which was Philip Merwarth’s Strategic Engine software in 2013. Unfortunately, they weren’t open-source. Worse was that the protocol for programming the Strategic Commander wasn’t documented anywhere online in a way that was accessible for users. This is why Weis realized that he could make a unique contribution.

It has been revealed that "I polished my old prototype code for the Strategic Commander software patch and released it as a library, so that other people could use it to write their own applications for programming the tool," he says. "As for me, I released one application that made use of the library publicly, the vJoy feeder application, which allows the device to be used with games that support joystick inputs." Curiously, Weis, by this time and like many others, had found other applications for a device with such a specific selling point, and even continues to use the Strategic Commander sparingly in 2026.

Industry observers note that "The production quality of Microsoft hardware at the time was just top-notch, and I love the design of the old SideWinder devices, which is why I did not just throw the thing out when the software stopped working," he tells me. "It was worth keeping around to find new uses for it over the years, and I eventually realized that it makes quite a nice addition to a HOTAS (Hands-On Throttle And Stick) setup, where I could put actions that aren’t time-critical and don't fit well on the throttle on the Strategic Commander instead. For example, when I’m playing Elite Dangerous in VR, I’d put actions like deploying the landing gear on the Strategic Commander to free up buttons on the throttle for actions that were more relevant for combat.".

Sources indicate that when looking back at the history of Microsoft’s SideWinder line, it’s easy to call the Strategic Commander a failed experiment, given the fact that most of us are still using the same standard mouse-and-keyboard setup to play RTS games. However, the central premise behind its design philosophy was that the interface between a player and a game could be redesigned to cater to specific genre quirks, and decades following its release, it’s still maintained a coalition of loyal consumers: some RTS players who believed the Strategic Commander really pulled it off, and those found other uses for the device in other flavours of PC game. And with the issue of modern compatibility, a roadblock for so much retro hardware, bypassed by homemade patches, both camps can continue twisting and clicking their Strategic Commanders unimpeded.

In a recent development, all the same, I wonder if it might have basked in more conventional success, had Microsoft made more forward-thinking decisions. The Strategic Commander has proven over the years that its unprecedented customisation had applications far beyond what Ledbetter’s team had envisioned, and once the popularity of RTS games settled down, other, similar click-heavy subgenres like MOBAs and Real-Time Tactics got significant as well. Would a more officially maintained, potentially refined Strategic Commander model have served those crowds? I think it might. The narrow focus on RTS games may have also hurt the device's since-demonstrated broader appeal; if Microsoft had fully capitalised on this customisation selling point by communicating its benefits to everyone, not just those playing the single most popular PC genre at the time, it could have provided the blueprint for a proper, long-lived alternative to controllers, mice, and keyboards.

Sources indicate that alas, gaming history is littered with revolutionary peripherals that failed to actually revolutionise the industry surrounding them. The Strategic Commander is no different, but for the fact that it’s had this surprisingly long post-shelf life - and, as a result, the opportunity for insight into what could have been done to salvage the its failures. Still, that unexpected longevity can provide come comfort to the Strategic Commander's creators, as well as its lingering consumers.

It has been revealed that "I think the design made sense for its time, especially with the rising popularity of RTS games," Ledbetter reflects. "Looking back, I would have liked more time to test and refine the Strategic Commander. I’m proud of what we brought to market, and I’m glad to know that it remains beloved by many players to this day.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • America's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission.
  • America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

America's electricity needs are growing rapidly, but the nation's aging power grid is struggling to keep up. More electric vehicles, increased electricity use in heavy industry, and the explosive growth of data centers are driving demand higher, putting additional pressure on an infrastructure system that is already falling behind.

Recent findings suggest that in a Policy Forum paper published in Science, energy policy researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and the University of California San Diego warn that the United States faces one of the world's most serious bottlenecks in electricity transmission. The problem could have major consequences for electricity prices, grid reliability, and the nation's economic future.

America Is Building Just 10% of the Power Lines It Needs.

According to recent reports, A major concern is the extremely slow pace of transmission construction. Over the past five years, the continental United States has added an average of only about 500 miles of high-voltage transmission lines annually. Research suggests the country needs approximately 5,000 miles each year to triple the size of its interregional transmission network by 2050 and accommodate future electricity demand.

That means the U.S. is building latest high-voltage transmission lines at just one-tenth of the estimated pace needed.

High-voltage transmission lines serve as the highways of the electricity system, carrying large amounts of power over long distances from generating facilities to communities and businesses. Connecting regional grids allows electricity to flow more easily between areas, helping balance supply and demand when local power production falls short.

Studies have shown that larger, better-connected electricity networks can reduce costs for consumers while also lowering the risk of catastrophic blackouts. When one region experiences a power shortage, electricity from another region can help keep the lights on.

Despite these advantages, expanding the nation's transmission infrastructure has proved extraordinarily difficult.

The Biggest Obstacle Isn't Technology.

In a recent development, according to the researchers (Madeline Yozwiak, David G. Victor, and M. Granger Morgan), the main barriers to modernizing America's power grid are political and regulatory rather than technological.

In a recent development, responsibility for approving major transmission projects is divided among federal agencies, state governments, local authorities, and private companies. Each has its own priorities and interests, creating numerous opportunities for proposed power lines to be delayed or blocked.

It has been revealed that existing electric utilities can also have financial reasons to resist stronger connections between regions. Greater competition from electricity suppliers elsewhere could weaken their influence over local markets, reducing the incentive to support projects that would benefit the broader electricity system.

As a result, even transmission projects that could lower costs and improve reliability across the country can struggle to gain approval.

Three Ways to Fix America's Power Grid Crisis.

To address the growing shortfall, the researchers recommend a three-part strategy combining stronger government action, modern transmission technologies, international cooperation, and regulatory reform.

Sources indicate that 1. Make better use of existing federal powers and advanced technologies.

In a recent development, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and the Department of Energy (DOE) already have legal authorities that could help move notable transmission projects forward. The researchers argue that these agencies should use those powers more effectively, including identifying transmission corridors of national importance and addressing disputes that prevent projects from receiving state-level approval.

Technological improvements could also dramatically increase the amount of electricity the grid can carry. One approach, known as reconductoring, involves replacing existing power line conductors with more advanced materials capable of transmitting more electricity without necessarily requiring entirely new routes.

Other advances, including newer High-Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) systems, offer additional ways to move large amounts of electricity efficiently. The researchers suggest that modern transmission technologies could double or even triple capacity.

According to recent reports, underground high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables offer another promising option. These systems can carry substantial amounts of electricity over long distances and could potentially be installed along existing highways and railroad corridors. Using these established routes could help avoid some of the land-use disputes and approval challenges that often delay conventional transmission projects.

Industry observers note that 2. Learn from countries that have already overcome similar obstacles.

The United States trails several international counterparts in building long-distance HVDC infrastructure and coordinating electricity transmission across regional and national boundaries.

Other countries have demonstrated that large transmission projects can move forward despite complicated political approval processes. Some have also successfully deployed underground HVDC systems on a large scale.

It has been revealed that rather than developing every solution independently, the researchers suggest that the U.S. should study these international experiences and adapt approaches that have already proved successful.

One proposal is to establish an international forum involving electricity regulators and other experts, potentially led by organizations such as the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC). Such a forum could help American policymakers identify effective regulatory practices, planning strategies, and technologies used elsewhere.

3. Create a national commission to break the political deadlock.

The researchers also recommend establishing a Presidential-Congressional Transmission Commission to address the political and regulatory conflicts that have slowed grid expansion for decades.

Modeled on previous successful bipartisan commissions, the proposed group would bring together key stakeholders to negotiate difficult decisions and develop a coordinated strategy for reform.

Its responsibilities would include recommending changes to state and federal laws, examining whether FERC should receive broader authority over the locations of newly introduced transmission projects, and developing financial incentives for companies that lead new construction.

The commission could also recommend financial rewards for communities that host transmission infrastructure, helping ensure that local residents share in the benefits of projects that serve larger regions.

Why America's Power Grid Crisis Could Get Worse.

Industry observers note that the researchers emphasize that the underlying challenge is not a lack of engineering solutions. Instead, the country's divided decision-making system allows individual stakeholders to obstruct projects that could deliver substantial nationwide benefits.

It has been revealed that "The fundamental challenge isn't technical, it's jurisdictional. Authority is divided among federal, state, and private entities, each with distinct priorities. When every stakeholder possesses the power to say no, even high-value projects that benefit the entire nation struggle to move forward," the authors warn.

Their assessment suggests that simply continuing with the existing system of overlapping regulations and fragmented authority will not be enough to meet America's growing electricity needs.

Without meaningful changes to how transmission projects are planned, approved, and built, the United States risks a prolonged infrastructure shortfall. The researchers warn that failing to resolve these problems could weaken electricity reliability and inflict lasting damage on the national economy, even as demand for power continues to climb.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the prayers of Final Fantasy old heads were finally answered this year with the release of Final Fantasy Resonance, a particularly retro-feeling entry in the franchise. Between the real-time battle system and 2.5D aesthetic, it's a throwback in the best way, and fans embraced it wholeheartedly, so much so, even the devs were surprised.

According to recent reports, "I think the action-oriented and 3D Final Fantasy games are wonderful too," Keisuke Nakashima, producer on Resonance, told Game*Spark, as translated by Automaton. "But I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of Final Fantasy they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art.".

I'm a member of noted corner of the overall fandom. Much as I enjoyed the huge, sleek main entries, my heart yearns for games that look and feel like the SNES installments, but with contemporary flavor. That's what Resonance delivers.

"We figured it was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," Nakashima adds. That's always a good starting point, and the devs figured correctly, although there was some concern over just how much it stood out amid the slate otherwise.

According to recent reports, "I expected opinions on it might be divided," Hiroto Furuya, director of Resonance, commented in the same interview. "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it.".

You and I both. Fans of the long-running role-playing juggernaut have had plenty to enjoy the last while. Besides Resonance, Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth continued the trilogy's blockbuster redux of the classic game, and Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles resurrected a fan-favorite for modern systems.

Final Fantasy Resonance is itself a top-down remake of aspects of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, a mobile game from 2015. I'm willing to bet most who checked out this version glossed over the original. It's probably safe to get moving on a follow-up that draws from further parts of the narrative in Exvius.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year.
  • It has been revealed that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a latest motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

Recent findings suggest that the class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

It has been revealed that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a latest motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

It has been revealed that "But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

Sources indicate that you know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which currently looks likely to last until at least 2028.

#143835. A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1586 w)

A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open upcoming possibilities for quantum technology.
  • Industry observers note that the material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented.
  • The discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A surprisingly simple metal has revealed an unusual form of magnetism that could open upcoming possibilities for quantum technology. Researchers have found compelling evidence of a rare magnetic state in which electrons behave in unexpected ways, even though the material produces no overall magnetization.

Industry observers note that the material, known as europium silicide (EuSi), contains an intricate magnetic structure that influences how electrons move and how their spins are oriented. This behavior is associated with a phenomenon called p-wave magnetism, an emerging area of research that could eventually help scientists develop fresh approaches to controlling electronic properties.

The discovery is particularly significant because EuSi is a relatively simple metallic compound. Unlike many materials previously considered for studying this exotic form of magnetism, it offers researchers a practical way to investigate the underlying physics in detail.

An Unexpected Discovery in a Simple Metal.

In a recent development, the research began about three years ago at the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids (MPI CPfS) in Dresden, Germany. Dr. Erjian Cheng successfully grew high-quality single crystals of EuSi, providing the material needed for detailed experiments.

When researchers first examined the crystals using photoemission techniques, which probe the energies and behavior of electrons inside materials, they noticed something unexpected. The magnetic arrangement of the atoms had a remarkably strong influence on the electronic band structure, which describes the energy levels electrons can occupy and helps determine how a material conducts electricity.

According to recent reports, that observation raised an intriguing possibility. Could this simple compound contain an unconventional form of magnetism in which the spin of an electron is connected to the direction it travels?

According to recent reports, "When we first measured the electronic structure of EuSi, we were surprised by the exceptionally large effect of magnetism on the electrons," explains Cheng. "That observation led us to investigate whether this simple compound could host a much more unusual magnetic state. The combination of crystal growth, neutron scattering and spin-resolved spectroscopy now provides compelling evidence for p-wave magnetism.".

Recent findings suggest that answering that question required an international collaboration involving 38 scientists from 19 institutions. Participants included researchers from ShanghaiTech University, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, the Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

A Strange Form of Magnetism That Cancels Itself Out.

Ordinary magnets, such as those attached to refrigerators, typically rely on a magnetic arrangement called ferromagnetism. In these materials, many electron spins align in the same direction, producing an overall magnetic field.

At temperatures between approximately 33 and 62 kelvin, the magnetic moments of its europium atoms organize themselves into a repeating spiral pattern. These temperatures correspond to roughly minus 400 to minus 348 degrees Fahrenheit.

It has been revealed that each europium atom has a substantial magnetic moment, but their orientations balance one another across the spiral. As a result, the material has no net magnetization in this magnetic phase.

However, the absence of overall magnetization does not mean magnetism has stopped influencing the electrons. In fact, the researchers found that the spiral arrangement produces a highly unusual electronic structure.

Industry observers note that in the proposed p-wave magnetic state, electrons traveling in opposite directions have opposite spin polarizations. Electron spin is a quantum property that gives electrons magnetic characteristics, although it should not be understood as an electron literally spinning like a tiny ball.

Recent findings suggest that the relationship between an electron's direction of motion and its spin is called an odd-parity spin texture. This means that reversing the electron's momentum also reverses the associated spin polarization.

Other materials can display spin-dependent energy differences because of a phenomenon known as spin-orbit coupling, which connects an electron's motion to its spin. In EuSi, however, the unusual spin structure appears to arise mainly from interactions between magnetic moments and the specific symmetry of their spiral arrangement.

Experiments Reveal Evidence of Rare P-Wave Magnetism.

To determine whether EuSi truly exhibits the predicted magnetic state, the scientists combined several sophisticated experimental methods with theoretical calculations.

First, they used neutron diffraction, a technique that reveals how atoms and magnetic moments are arranged inside a material. These measurements confirmed that the europium magnetic moments form a spiral structure with the symmetry required for p-wave magnetism.

Next, the researchers examined the material using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. This method measures the energies and momenta of electrons, allowing scientists to map the electronic structure.

The results highlighted that magnetic ordering substantially reorganizes the electron energy levels. In particular, the team observed magnetically driven energy separations exceeding 100 millielectronvolts, indicating an unusually strong influence of magnetism on electron behavior.

The most decisive evidence came from spin-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which allowed the researchers to examine electron spin polarization directly.

They observed that the sign of the spin polarization changed across successive magnetic Brillouin zones. These zones are regions of momentum space used by physicists to describe how electrons behave within a repeating magnetic structure.

The team also found that spin polarization became much weaker near locations where theoretical calculations predicted the p-wave spin texture should disappear.

Taken together, the measurements provide compelling experimental evidence consistent with the predicted p-wave magnetic state in EuSi.

A Hidden Magnetic Spiral With Two Different Orientations.

The researchers uncovered another unusual feature of EuSi involving chirality, a scientific term describing handedness.

Sources indicate that A familiar example is the difference between a left hand and a right hand. They are mirror images, but they cannot be perfectly superimposed.

Something similar happens with the magnetic spiral inside EuSi. Although the underlying crystal has a centrosymmetric structure, meaning its atomic arrangement is unchanged by inversion through a central point, the magnetic spiral can twist in either of two opposite directions.

These different spiral orientations create magnetic regions, or domains, with opposite handedness.

Using magnetic force microscopy and spatially resolved photoemission spectroscopy, the scientists identified domains measuring approximately ten micrometers across. For perspective, ten micrometers is about one-tenth the thickness of a typical human hair.

When the researchers examined these regions using circularly polarized light, they detected different electronic responses depending on the handedness of the magnetic spiral.

This finding demonstrates that the direction in which the magnetic structure twists is linked to the material's electronic properties.

Recent findings suggest that "What makes EuSi particularly exciting is that an unconventional electronic spin structure emerges from the magnetic order of a chemically simple metal," states Prof. Claudia Felser, Director at MPI CPfS. "This demonstrates how the discovery of newly introduced materials can reveal entirely new electronic phenomena. EuSi now gives us an experimental platform to investigate how magnetic symmetry and chirality can be used to control electronic properties, with potential implications for future spintronics and unconventional superconductivity.".

Why This Discovery Matters for Quantum Technology.

One of the biggest challenges in studying p-wave magnetism has been finding materials that display the necessary magnetic properties while remaining practical for detailed experiments.

Earlier candidates have included insulating materials, as well as metals that develop the required magnetic order only at extremely low temperatures or have complicated symmetries that make their behavior difficult to interpret.

EuSi offers a particularly useful combination of characteristics.

Industry observers note that it is a stoichiometric metal, meaning its constituent elements occur in a fixed chemical ratio. Researchers can also grow high-quality single crystals of the material, and its spiral magnetic arrangement has the symmetry associated with p-wave magnetism.

Together, these features make EuSi a promising experimental platform for exploring how exotic magnetic states influence the behavior of electrons.

According to recent reports, theoretical studies suggest that metallic p-wave magnets could display several remarkable properties. For example, they may allow electrons with particular spin orientations to carry electrical currents without requiring an external magnetic field.

They could also produce strong changes in spin polarization when an electric current is applied, potentially offering latest ways to manipulate electronic behavior.

These possibilities are especially relevant to spintronics, a field of technology that seeks to use electron spin, rather than electrical charge alone, to process and store information.

Another intriguing possibility involves unconventional superconductivity, in which electrical current flows without resistance through superconducting states that differ from those found in conventional superconductors.

It has been revealed that importantly, these predicted effects have not yet been demonstrated in EuSi. The discovery does not establish that the material can already perform these functions, but it gives researchers a promising system in which to test the predictions.

More broadly, the findings highlight how much of a material's behavior can remain hidden beneath an apparently simple chemical composition.

According to recent reports, A solid's properties depend on more than the elements it contains or how its atoms are positioned. The arrangement of magnetic moments, the symmetries they create, and the quantum behavior of electrons can also produce entirely unexpected effects.

By revealing compelling evidence of p-wave magnetism in EuSi, researchers have gained a fresh opportunity to investigate these relationships and explore how unusual magnetic structures might eventually be used to control the electronic properties of future materials.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto 6 map is massive - big enough to fit multiple maps from previous games inside of it.
  • However, you probably haven’t discovered many of the hidden secrets this new location has to offer.
  • For instance, have you discovered the alien hidden within the bunker?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto 6 map is massive - big enough to fit multiple maps from previous games inside of it. With a map that big, there are bound to be a lot of hidden details. If you’ve been exploring Leonida, you may have found some of them.

However, you probably haven’t discovered many of the hidden secrets this new location has to offer. There are hidden missions and interactions that might blow your mind.

For instance, have you discovered the alien hidden within the bunker? Maybe you haven’t been out to sea yet to find the kraken. There’s plenty to discover in this strange area.

It has been revealed that deep in Pelican Valley, you can find an abandoned research center. This is the strange part; that comes when you are inside. The strange part is that when you step inside, you will get assaulted by a giant crab, which is something straight out of a horror movie.

Sources indicate that this is a great easter egg in GTA 6, that connects the game to a movie from the 1980s called Island Claws. In this movie, a scientist breeds giant crabs, and then everything goes completely wrong.

Well, a scientist in GTA 6 tried doing the same thing, and it ended up breeding a giant crab that killed everyone, and now it is coming for you.

Once you have made your way to the Starlet Motel in Kelly County, head northwest. Locate the abandoned car with the flashing lights. From here, follow the path into the woods and you will discover a lady being abducted by a UFO. It is a wild sight.

Sources indicate that A few days later, go to sleep as the character you were playing as when you found the UFO. This will trigger a dream sequence where you need to sneak around alien eggs. It also gives you a look at the universe.

In a recent development, the whole dream sequence ends with you inserting a serum into a computer. I don’t want to give too much away, but it gets wild and there are cows involved.

There is a strange case that takes you to an alternate dimension in GTA 6. In reality, it seems more like it makes you trip extremely hard, but either way it is out of this world. It all starts by going to a construction site in Millport.

Inside one of the shipping containers here, you will find a mysterious case that you can interact with, though the name of the item is listed as “???.”.

Sources indicate that from here, get ready to be sent on a wild trip where you need to do a lot of parkour. You basically walk through various shipping containers and reach an area where you must parkour your way to victory. It isn’t just parkour, as you will need to swim at certain points, but it is a trip you won’t forget.

According to recent reports, after you have completed the alien abduction event and had one of the weirdest dreams of your life, it is time to rescue an alien from an underground bunker. Once the dream sequence is done, head to Mariana County, just south of Hamlet.

Here, you can find an old secret base. You will need to break in and climb down the ladder to get inside. Type in the code, access the building, and follow the corridors like you did in your dream.

You will need to put in sequences and everything, but in the end, you will be rewarded by seeing a real alien, and you can even help it escape the base so that it can return home.

According to recent reports, you may have spotted Skunkape during one of the earlier missions in GTA 6. During your time in Grassrivers, you can spot a creature running across the road. If you choose to follow it, it will disappear, and you may be wondering where it went.

Well, if you continue your search, you can find effigies that look similar to Bigfoot, but this is not Bigfoot. It is another creature known as Skunkape. When you turn away from the effigy, you will get hit from behind, and a cutscene will play.

In a recent development, after you have this encounter, you can go to Skeeter’s Bar in Hamlet and begin a mission for someone who is looking for the Skunkape. It is something you definitely don’t want to miss.

In Grand Theft Auto 5, you could get stuck out in the ocean, and it would require you to swim for a long time to get back to shore. It was very inconvenient, and so players probably aren’t very interested in getting stuck out at sea in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that well, if you decide to go far out into the ocean and wait for a while, you will get rescued by a dog that is driving a jet ski. It is quite odd, but an amazing interaction that you can certainly miss if you never go out of your way to be stranded in the ocean.

It has been revealed that the dog will also bring you to an island where there are other dogs, and it will also dig up some treasure for you. At least you don’t go home empty handed for all this work.

You can go searching for treasure in many different locations around Leonida. One of the best places is deep in the ocean, as you can find gold doubloons and more. However, there are some treasures around the map that come straight from space.

Sources indicate that if you search around Mount Kalaga, you can find what appears as purple mist. This is an impact crater, and it is one of the few sites where you can find a meteorite that has crashed into the ground.

While a space rock is cool, the best part about it is that you can sell it for a fair amount of money, so you will want to keep it on your person and take it to a pawn shop to get rid of it.

In a recent development, something that the game doesn’t tell you is that there are cocaine flamingos, which is a term I never thought I would write, but welcome to GTA 6. There are 125 cocaine flamingos scattered around Leonida, and you need at least 100 of them to complete a task.

You can go the entire game without realizing these statues exist, but if you pay attention, you will notice that these lawn ornaments are different from the standard ones found in many lawns.

Instead of having the standard black and yellow beak, cocaine flamingos have a black and white beak. These flamingo ornaments can be destroyed to find bricks of cocaine that you can sell to a dealer.

There are many different strange finds that you can discover under the surface of the ocean. Treasures galore wait for you in the deep, but so do monsters. Thankfully, they aren’t alive, unless you count a shark as a monster.

To the southeast of Gloriana Key, you can find a shipwreck. However, this is no ordinary shipwreck, as it was destroyed by none other than the mythical beast known as The Kraken.

The Kraken’s tentacles are wrapped all around the ship, which reminds me of Pirates of the Caribbean. Keep in mind that you need to swim very deep to find this hidden secret, and it may take a while to spot thanks to how dark the ocean can be.

Industry observers note that there is a hotel that is run by The Kingfishers in GTA 6, but they unfortunately aren’t having a great day. This hotel is located in Pelican Bay, and you want to be careful when you go here, as there is a tiger.

When you approach the hotel room, you will hear gunshots. If you make your way over to the area, you will see a massacre, as a tiger is loose around the area and is eating the various gang members.

It is a crazy interaction that is never marked on your map until you are nearby, so make sure you search the entirety of Pelican Bay and don’t miss anything.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

It has been revealed that the developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

In a recent development, starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

It has been revealed that speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese Upcoming Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

Industry observers note that on top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab notes you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

Industry observers note that you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with upcoming 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic.
  • It has been revealed that this new mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on.
  • As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star.

Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

It has been revealed that this new mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an glitch for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming update, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

According to recent reports, the findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

Recent findings suggest that psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood.

Sources indicate that to investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

It has been revealed that in studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis owners experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

In a recent development, the largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis users experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age.

Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, noted the findings raise crucial questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

Industry observers note that "We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large said. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine.".

Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis users and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

Sources indicate that however, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis users face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

"There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large remarked.

Industry observers note that the researchers also stressed an notable limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

Nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

"But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis.".

Fresh Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25.

The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

Sources indicate that in a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis people. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

By incorporating a much larger body of research, the upcoming analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, mentioned the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

Industry observers note that "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens said.

"There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is notable, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone.".

Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter.

Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

According to recent reports, the late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these important milestones.

"People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens said.

Prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

"It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he mentioned. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline.".

The potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings.

Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

In a recent development, "We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large stated. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met.".

One concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large noted its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

"It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk.".

Industry observers note that another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

In a recent development, at the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

Industry observers note that "You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large said.

More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure.

The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis customers, an increasingly important population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

Another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

Ultimately, the new analysis highlights an important gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

According to recent reports, this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

According to recent reports, of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

It has been revealed that critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

  • The fresh Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek – the one behind the likes of Half-Life 2, Portal and its sequel, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, and even Counter-Strike: Global Offensive – thinks GTA 6 is great… because you choose how to play. A fact that's lost on players complaining about optional missions.

The fresh Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date. However, there's still a vocal (minority, I'd like to think) group of players dismissing it as a game that forces some sort of agenda upon you. Faliszek covers this in his YouTube video on the "moral yellow paint," so to speak, of GTA 6.

According to the Valve veteran, there's no real reason for folks to complain about menial tasks like painting the house as Jason or buying flowers, even if "the game notes you're getting some kind of points or… gives you this list.".

While other games use yellow paint to give you set boundaries to stay within, in GTA 6 you can stray in whatever direction you'd like and play how you wish.

Sources indicate that in Faliszek's case, that means, uh, "bringing back bodies" and filling the house with corpses. It's all just GTA, after all.

"Now, would I do that in normal life? Does that make me a horrible person? Maybe. Does that make me a psycho in the game? Who cares?" As he says, "This is Grand Theft Auto." So, go on and ditch the chores to commit mass murder (if you please, of course). The writer notes that, again, it's all part of the game's sandbox elements – and, on that point, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 such a stand-out release.

In a separate short, Faliszek dubs GTA 6 "a masterpiece," saying, "it may be the greatest game ever made." He references other devs' criticism of Rockstar's fresh title – such as Warren Spector's, which argues he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – and dismisses it, reiterating that "it's an amazing game" and "incredible." I'm sure the freedom (to collect bodies, apparently) is a significant reason why.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

So, share in Faliszek's sentiment here and don't box yourself in with any preconceived "yellow paint" in GTA 6 when you don't have to. Clean the house, shower, buy gifts… or wreak havoc in Vice City and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours.

Industry observers note that the Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and remarked keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

The signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

Recent findings suggest that that spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko remarked on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a upcoming team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap rapidly.

Sources indicate that keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • In a recent development, from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

In a recent development, from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

In a recent development, it makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

Thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

Recent findings suggest that it's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock latest rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Recent findings suggest that between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make fresh, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that if you missed out on the Grand Theft Auto 6 pre-order bonuses, Rockstar is now offering the Vintage Vice City Pack as a standalone purchase. It's available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The DLC, which includes a classic car, a garage and some particularly nostalgic outfits, costs $4.99 in the US on both consoles.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar's original pre-order announcement, the pack was included with pre-orders of both editions of GTA 6, as well as digital purchases made before November 20. That meant you could still get the bonus if you bought the game on launch day. If you picked up your copy over the weekend instead, you'll have to pay for the extra content.

According to the official Xbox Store listing, the Vintage Vice City Pack went on sale as a separate add-on on November 20. It isn't a story expansion, but it does offer a little more than just cosmetic items for Jason and Lucia.

The most useful part of the pack is arguably the garage. It's located at Shore Court, near Ocean Beach, and comes with a weapon locker and storage space for goods you've stolen and intend to sell to a fence. You also get a 1955 Vapid Stanier, a classic sedan to keep in the garage. The extra garage alone might make the pack worthwhile if you like collecting cars in GTA.

The extra garage alone might make the pack worthwhile if you like collecting cars in GTA.

As for the cosmetic items, Jason gets a pastel linen suit and a retro haircut, while Lucia gets a short red sequin dress and curly hair. There's also a tropical weapon skin that you can apply to most firearms. The design is based on Tommy Vercetti's unmistakable Hawaiian shirt from GTA Vice City, which is a nice little detail for those of us who grew up playing that game.

In a recent development, the funny thing is that you can already unlock Tommy's original shirt in GTA 6 without buying anything extra. The catch is that it involves a rather elaborate Easter egg, so you might want to set aside some time for that one.

Before spending another five dollars on GTA 6, it's worth checking whether you already own the pack. The outfits, vehicle and garage don't all become available the moment you start the game. You'll have to reach certain points in Jason and Lucia's story before you can claim them.

Sources indicate that rockstar published a support article on November 24 explaining how to access the pre-order rewards. Bring up the pause menu, head to the Store section and find the Vintage Vice City Pack. Selecting an individual reward will tell you what you need to do to unlock it, so you don't have to guess which chapter you should be in. Once you've met the requirements, you'll have to return to the game itself to claim the reward. The Store menu tells you how to get it rather than handing you the items directly.

You don't need the Ultimate Edition to use the Vintage Vice City Pack, either. If you bought the Standard Edition on launch day, for instance, you should check your existing rewards rather than assume the pack is exclusive to the more expensive edition. It's sold separately from the Ultimate Edition Upgrade, and the latter has its own selection of unlockable vehicles, clothing and weapons.

GTA 4 gave us two excellent single-player expansions in The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, and we never got anything comparable for GTA 5 despite its ridiculously long lifespan.

Hopefully, Rockstar has something more substantial planned for GTA 6's single-player DLC. As much as I appreciate the nods to Vice City, I'd love to see the series return to the kind of expansions we got with GTA 4.
