💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peppermint oil, best known for its refreshing flavor and soothing effects on digestion, may also offer a surprising benefit for people with mildly elevated blood pressure.
  • Researchers at the University of Lancashire found that consuming a small amount of peppermint oil each day for just 20 days significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (the top number in a blood pressure reading).
  • The findings, published in the journal PLOS One, suggest that peppermint oil could provide a simple, inexpensive, and well-tolerated way to help manage mildly elevated blood pressure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peppermint oil, best known for its refreshing flavor and soothing effects on digestion, may also offer a surprising benefit for people with mildly elevated blood pressure.

Researchers at the University of Lancashire found that consuming a small amount of peppermint oil each day for just 20 days significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (the top number in a blood pressure reading). Participants who received peppermint oil had systolic readings that were an average of 8.5 mmHg lower than those who received a placebo after accounting for their starting blood pressure.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One, suggest that peppermint oil could provide a simple, inexpensive, and well-tolerated way to help manage mildly elevated blood pressure.

Recent findings suggest that lead author Dr. Jonnie Sinclair, Reader in Sport and Health Sciences, remarked: "High blood pressure is one of the biggest causes of heart disease and death worldwide, and it costs a huge amount of money to treat. Although medicines are commonly used to treat it, it's not always clear how well they work in the long-term, and they can cause unwanted side effects.".

How Peppermint Oil May Lower Blood Pressure.

Peppermint naturally contains several biologically active compounds, including menthol, which gives the plant its distinctive cooling sensation, and flavonoids, a group of plant compounds known for their antioxidant properties.

In a recent development, peppermint also has anti-inflammatory and vasodilatory properties, meaning it may help blood vessels relax and widen. When blood vessels widen, blood can flow more easily, potentially reducing the pressure exerted against artery walls. These properties may help explain peppermint oil's effects on blood pressure, although the precise mechanisms require further investigation.

Recent findings suggest that to examine these potential benefits, researchers recruited 40 adults between the ages of 18 and 65 with elevated blood pressure or stage 1 hypertension, an early stage of high blood pressure. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups.

One group consumed a total of 100 microliters of food-grade peppermint oil each day, equivalent to one-tenth of a milliliter, divided into two doses diluted in water. The other group received a peppermint-flavored placebo that contained none of the active peppermint oil compounds.

Significant Blood Pressure Improvements in Just 20 Days.

It has been revealed that after 20 days, average systolic blood pressure among participants taking peppermint oil fell from approximately 130 to 122 mmHg. Meanwhile, blood pressure remained virtually unchanged in the placebo group.

It has been revealed that systolic blood pressure measures the force of blood against artery walls when the heart contracts. Persistently elevated readings can damage blood vessels over time and increase the risk of serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure.

Although systolic blood pressure was the primary focus of the study, researchers also examined body measurements, blood test results, diastolic blood pressure (the bottom number in a blood pressure reading), resting heart rate, mental well-being, and sleep quality.

A Promising, Low-Cost Approach to High Blood Pressure.

Dr. Sinclair added: "Our findings were very positive and they have significant clinical implications, especially given arterial hypertension is the most common preventable risk factor for cardiometabolic disease and the greatest single risk factor for global mortality.

"Peppermint oil is low in calories and price so it's proved to be a very simple and cost-effective solution to potentially treat millions of people around the world.".

In a recent development, while the results are encouraging, the study involved a relatively small number of participants and lasted less than three weeks. Larger and longer clinical trials will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist over time and whether peppermint oil could complement existing blood pressure treatments.

It has been revealed that the researchers used peppermint oil specifically intended for human consumption. The findings should not be interpreted as a reason to replace prescribed blood pressure medications or ingest essential oils that are not formulated for oral use.

Materials provided by University of Lancashire. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, diablo 4’s segment in the massive Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the fresh class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

It has been revealed that what we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s latest region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two latest endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

Industry observers note that war Prepares lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a newly introduced activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

The club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

His next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

That deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

— FNATIC (@FNATIC) November 17, 2026.

For the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

Sources indicate that the club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert claims Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The latest hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in New Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

According to recent reports, twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 launches officially in more regions of the world.

It has been revealed that if you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. You can also read the Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 guide for a full breakdown on all the details ahead of its launch in your region.

I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • Recent findings suggest that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

Tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in New York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

Recent findings suggest that for Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

According to recent reports, sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun new ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

Sources indicate that then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

In a recent development, you could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

They often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

Sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

Sources indicate that the latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: 10 Side Modes That Became Bigger Than the Game They Came From

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me.
  • The same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra.
  • Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I have always been enamored with the different ways that games have been brought to life, and Mods in particular have always felt magical to me. Someone, somewhere, loves a game so much that they start tinkering with it in their free time. Every now and then, that little side project ends up taking on a life of its own. Some of the biggest games in the world, including two of the biggest esports I write about, started out exactly like that.

The same goes for bonus modes and custom maps that were never meant to be more than a fun extra. A few devs probably thought it would be fun to include a little bit of an extra to fans, or had an idea with limited resources that they wanted to give a try. Some of them went on to get their own releases, others created entire genres, and a few of them quite frankly outshone the game they were tucked away in. And in the spirit of that, let's take a look at ten side modes that became bigger than the game they came from.

Right, before you are all coming for me with pitchforks: Gwent never actually became bigger than The Witcher 3, and I have no qualms about admitting that straight away. Very few things could. The hype around it was something else, though: people happily ignored the end of the world to sit in taverns and play cards with every merchant, blacksmith and innkeeper they came across, and CD Projekt Red clearly noticed.

Industry observers note that the standalone version, GWENT: The Witcher Card Game, is something fans eagerly awaited. It did, however, come with its own sets of issues. The version of Gwent it delivered displayed a few stark differences to the version people knew and fell in love with: It was free-to-play, quite competitive, and ultimately, a lot of fans simply never warmed to it. If you're after that original feeling, most people will point you towards Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales instead.

Industry observers note that still, a card game from inside an RPG becoming popular enough to get its own release almost never happens. CD Projekt Red supported it until the end of 2023, and even then, it handed the game over to the community rather than switching it off. It didn't quite live up to the hype, but it absolutely earned its place on this list.

The Stanley Parable really shouldn't work as well as it does. You're an office worker, a narrator tells you exactly what you're doing, and it's up to you whether you want to listen to him. It's one of the funniest games I know, and it started out as a free Half-Life 2 mod that Davey Wreden released in 2011.

Wreden wanted to play around with what storytelling in games could be, and it clearly struck a nerve: the mod was downloaded more than 90,000 times in just two weeks. William Pugh then reached out about turning it into something bigger, and the two of them spent the next two years working on it entirely online. They only met in person a month after it came out, which is a detail to the origin story that I personally find quite charming.

That remake released in 2013 and sold over 100,000 copies within a matter of days. Ultra Deluxe followed in 2022 and did the same within 24 hours.

Team Fortress 2 is so closely tied to Valve that it's easy to forget it didn't start there at all. It began as a Quake mod in 1996, made by three Australians, Robin Walker, John Cook and Ian Caughley, who had been inspired by a little Doom map they came across at LAN parties. Two teams, a bunch of very different classes, and everyone has a job to do. Sound familiar?

Valve liked it so much that it bought the rights and offered its creators jobs. Caughley said no, but Walker and Cook moved over, and Team Fortress Classic came out in 1999 as a mod for Half-Life. It then took until 2007 for Team Fortress 2 to finally arrive, with a cartoony art style that has aged better than most games from that year.

Once it went free-to-play in 2011, it became bigger and better. Somewhere between capturing the intelligence and pushing the payload, a huge part of the community became very, very invested in hats. I'm not judging, but I am a little bit scared of how much money has gone into them.

It has been revealed that as someone who writes about esports, the lore behind Dota is one of my favorite tidbits of the gaming world. It all started with Aeon of Strife, a custom StarCraft map, which inspired a modder called Eul to make Defense of the Ancients for Warcraft III all the way back in 2003. Eventually, Eul made it open-source, and from there, it passed from hand to hand.

The most popular version became DotA Allstars, made by Steve "Guinsoo" Feak, and when he moved on, the mysterious IceFrog took over. Guinsoo went on to help create League of Legends, which means one Warcraft III map is responsible for two of the biggest esports on the planet. What a wild family tree!

Sources indicate that valve hired IceFrog in 2009, Dota 2 came out in July 2013, and the rest is happily ever after: it has been one of the most played games on Steam ever since. Truth be told, I love that the person who has shaped Dota more than anyone is still somewhat of a mystery. Somehow, that makes the whole thing even more feel like classic Dota.

Sources indicate that counter-Strike is one of the most influential FPS games ever created, but it doubled as probably the most impressive job application to exist. Minh "Gooseman" Le was in his last semester at university and wanted something that would help him get into game development, so he started working on a mod for Half-Life. Jess "Cliffe" Cliffe ran the website and the community, and the first beta came out in June 1999.

Every fresh beta brought in more players, and by 2000, Valve had bought the rights and hired them both. From there, it was Source, Global Offensive and, in 2023, Counter-Strike 2, with the series becoming one of the biggest esports in the world along the way. Its Majors are still some of the biggest events in esports.

Sources indicate that counter-Strike 2 still regularly sits at the very top of Steam's charts, with over 30 million monthly players. Gooseman, for the record, definitely got the job. I'd say it worked out.

Industry observers note that there was a point where it felt like every other game had zombies in it, and DayZ was right at the heart of that. It started out in 2012 as a mod for Arma 2, made by Dean "Rocket" Hall, and threw you into a huge open world full of the undead. The zombies were never really the scary part, though: other players were, because you never knew whether the person waving at you wanted to team up or take your tinned food.

You needed Arma 2 to play the mod, so its popularity sent a three-year-old military sim right back to the top of Steam's charts. It reached a million players within four months, Hall joined Bohemia Interactive, and work began on a standalone version. Bohemia, quite understandably, was delighted.

That version debuted into Early Access in December 2013 and sold over two million copies in under six months, before its full release in 2018. I'll say this much: it hasn't moved all that far away from the mod, and that is a good thing. If you like survival games and don't mind a bit of betrayal, it's well worth your time.

It has been revealed that I’ll be honest, most of the Skyrim mods I personally perused have always been about silly things like turning every dragon into Thomas the Tank Engine. Those of you with more dignified taste, however, might be aware of The Forgotten City. It’s a time-travelling murder mystery set in an ancient underground city. Nick Pearce spent more than 1,700 hours on it, and it clearly was time well spent: the mod had over three million downloads, and an Australian Writers' Guild Award, the first time a video game had ever won one.

Pearce quit his job as a lawyer and rebuilt it as a standalone game with two other developers. It moved from Skyrim to ancient Rome, but kept its central idea: there is one rule, and if anyone breaks it, everybody pays. Steal from someone or hurt them, and the entire city is turned into gold.

Sources indicate that luckily, you get sent back to the start of the day whenever that happens, with everything you've collected so far. It's almost roguelike in that way, and every loop teaches you a little more about the people around you. I think it's one of the best detective games out there, and it started its life as a Skyrim mod.

It has been revealed that call of Duty: World at War was a very serious entry about the Pacific front of World War II, which is exactly why it's so funny that most people remember it for zombies. Treyarch hid Nacht der Untoten at the end of the campaign as an Easter egg, with no marketing behind it at all. You finished the story, and suddenly you were boarding up windows in a bunker whilst zombies tried to get in.

It was a hit straight away, so every map pack after that came with a new Zombies map. The first map didn't even have a story, but fans started building one anyway, and Treyarch eventually leaned all the way into it. The result is one of the most convoluted storylines in gaming, spread across multiple Black Ops games.

Zombies has been part of nearly every Call of Duty since, and these days, it's not unusual for it to be the main reason people pick up a Treyarch game at all. Quite the career for an Easter egg. Not even the developers saw that one coming.

According to recent reports, dota Auto Chess is the youngest entry on this list, and boy, did it blow up fast. Drodo Studio released it as a custom game inside Dota 2 in January 2019. You put Dota heroes on a chessboard, combine them to make them stronger and then sit back whilst they fight on their own, and the developers have actually stated that Mahjong was a big inspiration.

Within months, it had over eight million players, and the big studios very quickly wanted a piece of it. Valve made Dota Underlords, Riot added Teamfight Tactics to League of Legends, and Blizzard brought Battlegrounds to Hearthstone. Drodo Studio, meanwhile, released its own standalone Auto Chess.

Industry observers note that the hype has calmed down since then, but the auto battler genre is still very much here, and all of it traces back to one custom game. I find it quite funny that one of the biggest gaming trends of 2019 started out as just another option in Dota 2's custom games menu. Never underestimate a menu.

It has been revealed that the Binding of Isaac has a truly baffling amount of mods, and as someone that used to be utterly besotted with both the OG as well as The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, I have tried a large amount of them. A lot of them were high quality, but Antibirth was something else. Released by a group of fans in December 2016, it was basically an entire expansion: thousands of new rooms, nearly 100 new items and even its own soundtrack. It felt so much like Isaac that it was hard to believe it wasn't official.

Edmund McMillen clearly shared the fans’ feelings. He loved how well it understood the themes and style of his game, and rather than ignoring it, he started working with the team behind it. In 2018, he announced The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, the final DLC for the game, built on Antibirth.

According to recent reports, repentance launched in 2021, with the Antibirth team helping to make their mod official, alongside a whole lot of new content. I love that a fan project ended up becoming the final chapter of the game it was made for. Not many modders can say that.

#143791. Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1195 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A upcoming Stanford Medicine-led study has identified three distinct biological brain types, known as biotypes, in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety disorder or both conditions.
  • Sources indicate that the findings could help unravel the complicated relationship between two of the most common childhood mental health disorders, which frequently share symptoms.
  • It has been revealed that by examining thousands of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans, researchers identified three biological patterns associated with different groups of symptoms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming Stanford Medicine-led study has identified three distinct biological brain types, known as biotypes, in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety disorder or both conditions.

Sources indicate that the findings could help unravel the complicated relationship between two of the most common childhood mental health disorders, which frequently share symptoms. Published recently in Nature Mental Health, the study reveals that each biotype involves disruptions in a different set of brain circuits.

It has been revealed that by examining thousands of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans, researchers identified three biological patterns associated with different groups of symptoms. These findings could eventually help doctors recognize ADHD and anxiety earlier, identify new targets for treatment, and determine which therapies are most likely to benefit individual patients.

"The high overlap between ADHD and anxiety actually hinders our understanding of the neurobiology underlying traditional, symptom-based diagnoses," remarked co-senior study author Yu Zhang, PhD, assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences.

Recent findings suggest that doctors currently rely on symptom checklists to diagnose ADHD and anxiety. However, Zhang explained that children diagnosed with either disorder frequently experience symptoms associated with the other.

Looking Beyond Traditional ADHD and Anxiety Diagnoses.

In a recent development, yong Jiao, PhD, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Iowa, is the study's lead author. Zhang shares senior authorship with Jing Jiang, PhD, assistant professor of pediatric neurology at the University of Iowa.

"We wanted to know whether the biological differences among children with ADHD and anxiety follow the diagnostic labels used in the clinic," Zhang mentioned.

The researchers found that the relationship was not so straightforward. Children diagnosed with ADHD, anxiety or both could belong to any of the three brain biotypes, although some biological patterns were more prevalent among children with particular diagnoses.

According to the researchers, identifying these underlying differences could add a valuable layer of biological information to existing diagnostic categories, benefiting both future research and clinical care.

AI Uncovers Hidden Patterns in Thousands of Brain Scans.

The research team drew on data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, an ongoing investigation of brain development involving more than 11,000 children across the United States. Participants were 9 or 10 years old when they entered the project.

The analysis included 3,508 children who already had a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both when they enrolled, along with 693 children who initially had neither diagnosis but subsequently developed one or both conditions. Another 1,947 children who never received either diagnosis served as a control group.

All participants underwent fMRI brain scans and completed a series of cognitive and behavioral assessments. To independently validate their findings, the scientists examined brain scans from another 224 children participating in a separate research project called the Healthy Brain Network. Each child in this additional group had been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety disorder.

The team developed an artificial intelligence model to investigate functional connectivity, which describes how different regions of the brain work together. By incorporating diagnostic information and behavioral test results, the model identified patterns of brain connectivity that were more pronounced in children with ADHD, anxiety or both compared with those who had neither condition.

Combining behavioral information with brain imaging data revealed two major dimensions of dysfunction associated with ADHD and anxiety: cognitive-behavioral dysfunction and emotion-attention dysfunction.

It has been revealed that each dimension involves a different network of brain regions. Different combinations of these disruptions produced three distinct biotypes, which the researchers named the externalizing-disinhibited biotype, the internalizing-distressed biotype and the mixed biotype.

Three Distinct Brain Types and Their Symptoms.

The three biological categories were mutually exclusive (each child was in only one biotype), but none was limited to a particular traditional diagnosis.

Children belonging to the externalizing-disinhibited group tended to exhibit higher levels of impulsivity, hostility, defiance, aggression and rule-breaking behavior. ADHD diagnoses were more common among children in this group.

According to recent reports, the internalizing-distressed group was characterized by greater feelings of guilt and tension, stronger perfectionist tendencies, and more symptoms associated with anxiety and depression. Children with this biological profile were more frequently diagnosed with anxiety disorders.

Industry observers note that those in the mixed group experienced more difficulties with attention, irritability and self-injury. Like children in the externalizing-disinhibited group, they were more likely to have an ADHD diagnosis.

Despite these tendencies, researchers found every combination of brain biotype and conventional diagnosis among the children they studied.

Brain Changes Could Reveal ADHD and Anxiety Before Diagnosis.

One of the most surprising findings emerged when scientists examined brain scans taken from children who had not been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety when they first entered the study.

The distinctive biological patterns were already detectable in their initial scans, even though the children did not receive a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both until later.

"We think this means we may be able to use the biotypes as an early indicator of these conditions," Zhang said, noting that identifying these patterns before diagnosis was the most unexpected aspect of the research. "It could help us provide more timely intervention for these conditions and slow down or, we hope, even reverse their progression.".

Toward More Personalized ADHD and Anxiety Treatments.

Industry observers note that zhang does not expect the newly identified brain biotypes to replace conventional diagnoses based on symptoms. Instead, combining the two approaches could help clinicians select treatments that are better suited to individual children.

Finding an effective treatment for ADHD or anxiety currently involves considerable experimentation. Children may need to try several medications before discovering which one provides meaningful relief.

"When doctors prescribe a latest medication, it can take quite a long time -- a couple of weeks or months -- to see a response," Zhang said. "If the first medication doesn't work, they switch to a different one".

This process can be lengthy, expensive and frustrating.

Zhang hopes future clinical trials will build on the team's findings by investigating how different treatments affect specific patterns of brain activity. Such studies could eventually help researchers determine which therapies are most effective for each of the three biotypes.

"We want to find biomarkers that can really inform the right treatment at the right time," he said.

Researchers involved in the study are affiliated with Stanford University's Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute and the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI.

Additional contributors came from the University of Iowa, the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine.

The research received funding from the National Institutes of Health (grant numbers R01MH129694, R01MH136197, R01MH145082, R01MH140425, U24AA021697, R01DA057567, R37MH101495 and R01MH132784), the Eagles Autism Foundation, the Stanford Knight Initiative for Brain Resilience, the Rosenkranz Foundation, the Brain and Behavior Research Foundation, and the Effie and Wofford Cain Foundation.

According to recent reports, the first HBO Lego Harry Potter sets have been revealed, and they're remaking some classic kits... but fans aren't all enthused by the result.

After being teased earlier this year, the initial wave of Lego Harry Potter kits based on HBO's latest series revisits some old haunts; the lineup includes the Gryffindor Common Room, the Hogwarts Express, and Privet Drive. These include new designs and minifigures based on the TV show, but there are obviously similarities to what we've seen before – and that seems to be a sticking point for some. In a Reddit post discussing the sets, the top comment notes that they "they look like bootlegs of the originals lol.".

It has been revealed that while there's positive feedback as well (particularly toward Privet Drive's faux-Tudor design), I'm finding just as many negative responses on social media after a quick look through the likes of Instagram. These sets are clearly dividing the community, and I can't imagine it's the reception Lego was hoping for. Here are the kits themselves:.

It has been revealed that the Gryffindor Common Room is a constant throughout the Potter stories, so it makes sense that Lego would remake it here in its new HBO form. This one is made up of 738 pieces, comes with five minifigures (Harry, Ron, Hermione, Parvati, and Lavender), as well as lots of little details on almost every surface.UK: £79.99 at Lego.

This is probably the most unique of the sets, as the faux-Tudor exterior is quite different from the old movie version. The kit has 545 pieces and four minifigs to go with a brick-built '90s car – Harry, Uncle Vernon, Aunt Petunia, and Dudley. UK: £54.99 at Lego.

What with Harry's first trip to Hogwarts being such a pivotal moment in the story, it makes sense that the Hogwarts Express would feature as a major new set. This is just the latest in a long line of models recreating this train, and while the engine itself is practically identical, the HBO version of the platform looks like it includes a little cafe waiting area that we've not seen before.UK: £89.99 at Lego.

Industry observers note that the final set to be revealed thus far is a BrickHeadz kit, recreating characters in a larger scale. This one has Harry, Malfoy, and Hagrid presumably while they're wandering the Forbidden Forest in detention. It's made up of 380 pieces.UK: £22.99 at Lego.

Sources indicate that with Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

#143786. Industry News: Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging

Industry News: Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1012 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blood vessels naturally become less flexible with age, and certain diseases can accelerate this process.
  • It has been revealed that one factor that can contribute to this damage is an excess of phosphate in the bloodstream.
  • Sources indicate that scientists at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine have identified a kidney protein that plays a critical role in regulating blood phosphate levels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blood vessels naturally become less flexible with age, and certain diseases can accelerate this process. As blood vessels stiffen, the risk of cardiovascular disease and premature death increases.

It has been revealed that one factor that can contribute to this damage is an excess of phosphate in the bloodstream. Although elevated blood phosphate (hyperphosphatemia) is relatively uncommon in the general population, it occurs much more frequently in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD), whose kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste from the blood.

Sources indicate that scientists at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine have identified a kidney protein that plays a critical role in regulating blood phosphate levels. The discovery could have particularly key implications for people living with CKD.

In a fresh study published in October 2026, the researchers found that a deficiency of this protein caused blood vessels to stiffen more rapidly and shortened lifespan in animal models. These effects were especially pronounced when the animals consumed a diet high in phosphate. Reducing phosphate intake helped alleviate some of the damage.

According to recent reports, the findings point to a potential new target for medications and other therapies designed to maintain healthy phosphate levels. Such treatments could eventually help people with CKD improve their overall health and potentially live longer.

Recent findings suggest that "Phosphate is really underestimated in terms of longevity in all mammals. The higher the concentration of phosphate in the blood, the shorter the lifespan," indicates Makoto Miyazaki, PhD, a research professor in the Division of Renal Diseases and Hypertension and the senior author of the new study.

How Excess Phosphate Accelerates Blood Vessel Aging.

In a recent development, phosphorus is an essential nutrient that helps build and maintain strong bones. It occurs naturally in a wide variety of whole foods, including meat, poultry, fish, whole grains, nuts, legumes, and dairy products, generally in the form of organic phosphate compounds. Food manufacturers also add phosphates to processed foods and beverages to improve flavor and extend shelf life.

Although phosphorus is necessary for good health, excessive levels in the blood (hyperphosphatemia) can trigger a series of damaging biological changes. Phosphate additives may be particularly concerning because the body absorbs them more rapidly and efficiently than the organic phosphates naturally present in whole foods.

In a recent development, persistently elevated phosphate levels can cause smooth muscle cells within blood vessel walls to behave more like cells responsible for building bone. As a result, these cells begin depositing calcium phosphate crystals resembling those found in bones, causing the blood vessels to harden (or calcify).

Healthy blood vessels are flexible, allowing them to expand and contract in response to changing blood flow demands. Calcification compromises this flexibility, effectively accelerating vascular aging and potentially contributing to numerous age-related health problems throughout the body.

A Hidden Protein Helps Maintain Phosphate Balance.

Under normal circumstances, the kidneys remove excess phosphate from the bloodstream before it reaches harmful levels. As CKD progresses, however, declining kidney function makes it increasingly difficult for the body to eliminate phosphate and other substances.

According to recent reports, maintaining the right amount of phosphate requires continuous adjustments. After the kidneys filter phosphate from the blood, a portion is eliminated through urine, while the remainder is returned to the circulation. A protein known as NPT2A is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 75% of the filtered phosphate, preventing the body from losing too much phosphorus.

It has been revealed that when phosphate levels are already elevated, however, this recycling mechanism can become problematic. Miyazaki and his colleagues discovered that another protein, called TMEM174, acts as a natural brake on this process. By binding to NPT2A, it limits the amount of phosphate being reabsorbed into the bloodstream.

Protein Deficiency Shortens Lifespan in Animal Models.

The latest findings highlight the importance of TMEM174 in maintaining healthy phosphate levels. Animals deficient in the protein struggled to regulate phosphate in their blood, experienced increased vascular calcification, and had significantly shorter lifespans.

It has been revealed that "We don't fully understand how yet, but somehow TMEM174 is destabilizing NPT2A," claims Miyazaki. "And without enough TMEM174, homeostasis is disrupted.".

Sources indicate that A deficiency of TMEM174 appears to result primarily from genetic factors rather than chronic kidney disease itself. However, the research suggests that people with CKD who also have insufficient levels of this protein could be particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of excess phosphate.

A Potential Latest Target for Protecting Blood Vessels.

Miyazaki hopes the discovery will lead to treatments that reduce the amount of excess phosphate the kidneys return to the bloodstream.

Industry observers note that dietary changes may provide some benefit, particularly by reducing consumption of fast food, deli meats, sodas, and other processed products that contain large amounts of phosphate. However, Miyazaki explains that managing phosphate levels through diet alone can be challenging, especially for people with CKD. Because phosphate is present in such a wide range of foods, avoiding it is virtually impossible.

In future research, Miyazaki plans to investigate these kidney proteins further, along with the hormones involved in maintaining the body's chemical balance. He also wants to better understand why calcium accumulation in blood vessels is so common among people with CKD.

For now, identifying the role of TMEM174 represents an crucial advance in understanding how the body regulates phosphate. It could also help lay the groundwork for newly introduced approaches to improving the health of people whose phosphate balance is disrupted.

"Scientists have been studying phosphate homeostasis for over 100 years, so to still find a latest protein that regulates phosphate is kind of unique," indicates Miyazaki.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot newly introduced revision that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific problems, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for patch 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

Industry observers note that this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into challenges with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Recent findings suggest that team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s enhancement takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

According to recent reports, finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

Industry observers note that if you're a longtime reader, you may remember the launch of Torerowa, the Dark & Darker-like multiplayer dungeon crawler, back in 2025. And since then, it's been chugging along quite nicely, having now reached its 15th season! But what else could Torerowa have in store? Quite a lot, it seems.

Season 15 of Torerowa debuts today and includes many new layers to the dungeon, bringing the total depth to floor B35F. That means more loot, more monsters and more risk, but even more potential rewards too. However, that's just the tip of the iceberg, as this enhancement also sees the introduction of Guilds!

Speaking of socialising, there's also new places to visit in the form of the Adventurers' Tavern and the Workshop, the former of which is sure to be a big favourite with players, especially if you've played Dark & Darker and enjoyed the antics in the pre-match tavern lobby.

Recent findings suggest that outside of this new content, there's also plenty of intriguing, smaller additions such as the Treasure and Dress-Up Gachas, not to mention auto-translation for chat. All in all, it's a set of very exciting additions to Torerowa which, especially with Dark & Darker seemingly slipping out of the spotlight, makes this a great option for Tarkov-like dungeon crawling on mobile.

But if you'd prefer a more small-scale, personal journey in a fantasy world, then we can provide that too. Check out our list of the best RPGs on Android to see some of our choice picks which you can play right now!

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest enhancement post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by Upcoming Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Sources indicate that other than these newly introduced hires, the patch is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

The enhancement is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but Upcoming Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

Sources indicate that this one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

According to recent reports, the substantial new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Sources indicate that varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

Industry observers note that the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Industry observers note that outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the proposal or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for new ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

Industry observers note that it feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

In a recent development, luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

In a recent development, one example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from significant crime stories or not?

It has been revealed that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

It has been revealed that sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

According to recent reports, rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

There’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

In a recent development, in its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

According to recent reports, rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

In a recent development, when we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, indicated that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

The game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

According to recent reports, stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1158 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.
  • Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.
  • Latest research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.

Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.

Latest research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however. Between 2011 and 2022, the proportion of older adults with cognitive disorders taking medications that could impair their cognitive function decreased significantly.

After analyzing data from 2,796 older adults with cognitive disorders who lived independently, researchers found that exposure to potentially inappropriate medications fell from 39.3% in 2011 to 29.3% in 2022.

In a recent development, "This is a population with some mental challenges that relate to the central nervous system. These drugs also act on the central nervous system, so they can be too much for older adults if inappropriately used," says Haowen Hsu, PharmD, a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Pharmacy Practice at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and first author of the study, published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

Reducing the Risks of Common Prescription Drugs.

Older adults who have spent years taking benzodiazepines such as Xanax for anxiety or sleep medications such as Ambien may benefit from a medically supervised reduction in dosage or gradual discontinuation. These medications can negatively affect cognitive function, balance, and coordination.

In a recent development, "A central word for patients in this age group is 'deprescribing,' which means, for example, removing inappropriate medications and decreasing the frequency or the dosage. In some cases, it means replacing the current medication with a milder alternative," Hsu states. "This is why it's so vital for health care providers to work closely with community pharmacists and homecare nurses to optimize medication safety.".

To identify potentially problematic drugs, the research team consulted the American Geriatrics Society's Beers Criteria, which identifies approximately 100 medications that may pose risks to older adults. The researchers then concentrated specifically on medications that could present additional dangers for people with diagnosed cognitive disorders.

Using data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, the team examined a sample representing approximately 29.7 million older Americans with cognitive disorders over the period from 2011 to 2022. They compared individuals prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication with those who had not received any of these drugs.

Medication Safety Has Improved, but Risks Remain.

Although the study did not examine what caused the decline in exposure to potentially harmful medications, Hsu points to growing awareness among researchers and clinicians over the past two decades. The gradual but sustained improvement may reflect broader advances in geriatric medicine and efforts to make prescription drug use safer.

According to recent reports, "We were happy to see the percentages of harm decline over that 11-year period," he notes. "However, one-third of our target population is still exposed to these harmful medications, which isn't good.".

Recent findings suggest that older adults, even those without cognitive disorders, are particularly susceptible to harmful drug interactions and inappropriate prescriptions. In some cases, these complications can increase the risk of death. These dangers are a central focus of Team Alice, an ongoing interdisciplinary research initiative at the University at Buffalo dedicated to medication safety.

A Preventable Death Inspires Change.

According to recent reports, team Alice takes its name from Alice Brennan, who died in 2009 following a prescription for a muscle relaxant identified as potentially inappropriate under the Beers Criteria. The prescribing error went unrecognized within the health care system, and Brennan died following six weeks of preventable complications.

Her daughter, Mary Brennan-Taylor, shared her mother's experience with University at Buffalo researchers in the hope of bringing about systemic changes that would spare other patients and families from similar harm.

Hsu began the newly introduced study shortly after joining the university's pharmacy school and Team Alice, where he works in the UB Patient Safety Learning Laboratory.

"This work extends a series of national analyses our group has published on potentially inappropriate medications, quality of life, and health care use in older adults," claims David Jacobs, PharmD, PhD, associate professor of pharmacy practice and a principal investigator on Team Alice.

It has been revealed that "It is especially notable as older adults with cognitive disorders are the least able to tolerate medications that worsen memory or thinking, yet nearly one in three are still receiving them. Most of these patients have a regular source of care so these medications can be identified and addressed with their care team.".

Improving Medication Safety for Older Adults.

Other contributors to the study included Team Alice's fellow principal investigators Ranjit Singh, MD, associate professor and interim chair of the Department of Family Medicine at UB's Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and Robert Wahler, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice.

Collin Clark, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice, and Steven Feuerstein, an information systems analyst at the Jacobs School, also contributed to the research.

The findings underscore the value of thorough medication reviews during routine outpatient appointments. The researchers also suggest incorporating clinical assessment tools such as the Drug Burden Index into acute and outpatient care. Such tools can help health care professionals assess the combined effects of medications that act on the central nervous system and potentially prevent avoidable complications.

Further research is needed to establish whether improving medication use can enhance quality of life and reduce hospital admissions and emergency room visits among older adults experiencing cognitive difficulties.

A Rapidly Aging Population Raises New Concerns.

The findings arrive at a significant moment in global demographic history. According to a recent report from the U.S. Census Bureau, adults age 65 and older now outnumber children from birth through age 5 worldwide for the first time in human history.

However, greater longevity does not necessarily translate into more years of good health. The same report indicates that nearly 75% of adults age 65 and older have at least two chronic health conditions. Managing multiple illnesses often requires taking more medications, some of which may have detrimental effects on the aging body and brain.

In a recent development, "This is an issue that has been building for decades, but the growth of the older adult population has arrived sooner than we expected," Hsu says. "This means that health care professionals need to pay closer attention than ever to medication safety, especially for older adults experiencing cognitive decline or other complex health concerns.".

Latest Update: Nintendo Switch 2 Patent Paves Way For DS/Wii U Games
